articles.title: Laver Cup back in the balance as Team World match their captain Andre Agassi’s energy
articles.summary: Alex de Minaur recovers from match point down to beat Alexander Zverev. Carlos Alcaraz launches comeback of his own to leave event level at 5-5. For much of his afternoon on court against Alexander Zverev, Alex de Minaur seemed destined to end his day with an excruciating defeat.
body: No matter how grim the scoreline appeared, though, every effort he made was punctuated by roars of approval from one person in particular. There were loud screams of encouragement, pounding of chairs and stamping of feet. At one point, as doubt had crept into Zverev’s game during the second set tie-break, that unmistakable voice from the sidelines yelled out: “Check his oil! Check his oil!”

Those words came from Andre Agassi and, with such unconditional support provided by one of the greatest tennis players of all time, his Team World captain, there was no way that De Minaur could lose. De Minaur’s probing soon revealed that Zverev had indeed run out of oil, his engine failing, as the Australian recovered from match point down to close out a 2-6, 7-6 (5), 11-9 win.

Agassi’s unbridled enthusiasm and support was reflected in his team as they held their own on day two of the Laver Cup against a group of higher-ranked opponents. With Team Europe leading 3-1 overnight, Learner Tien of the US opened the day with a 6-3, 2-6, 10-7 win over the Italian Flavio Cobolli before De Minaur defeated Zverev, the recent French and US Open champion.

articles.title: Oyarzabal earns Spain Nations League win as England pay for Kane penalty miss
articles.summary: It was another high-profile game when Thomas Tuchel’s England let a lead slip in the second half and went on to lose. But unlike the last time, it was not one for recriminations. The England support can accept losing when their team plays with cut and thrust.
body: England were game. They were driven by Jude Bellingham, who ran on adrenaline and played to the point of maximum expression. They had positive surges either side of the interval, especially the one towards the end of the first half when goals from Anthony Gordon and Harry Kane put them in charge, hauling them back after Lamine Yamal’s second-minute goal.

The biggest takeaway was Spain’s slickness. There is a reason why they won the World Cup in the summer. Why they won the European Championship before that. They are the best team in the international game by a distance. Nobody can live with them. England did well to stay within a puncher’s chance of a result in this Nations League opener; Bellingham was still throwing them in stoppage time. Crucially, as Tuchel and England try to look forward after the heartbreak of the World Cup semi-final defeat against Argentina, there was no negativity from the Wembley crowd. Even in the face of England’s defending, which was dreadfully loose.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland’s Gavin Bazunu boycotts Israel match ‘as a person of principle’
articles.summary: Bolton goalkeeper issues statement after withdrawal. Ireland players will wear black armbands in match. The Republic of Ireland will fulfil their fixture against Israel in Hungary on Sunday night, but only after lengthy deliberations between the players resulted in a “significant majority” voting…
body: After a week in which the Irish team and officials have come under increasing domestic pressure to boycott the match due to Israel’s military actions in Gaza, training was delayed by five hours on Saturday while the squad discussed whether to go ahead.

“This morning, a player expressed their discomfort with fulfilling this fixture to the head coach and indicated their intent to withdraw from the squad,” said the FAI’s chief David Courell, referring to Bazunu.

“What proceeded was another four hours of conversations, predominantly amongst the players themselves, but also at times with the coaching staff and the executive. Ultimately we carried out a vote amongst the squad... and it was a significant majority that was returned with the intention to continue.”

Courell said the squad had also agreed a number of measures to signal their unease with the fixture taking place. Players are to wear black armbands “in recognition of all the lives lost in the conflict” he said, adding that there will be “elements of the pre-match ceremony” that will “not be partaken in by the Republic of Ireland” players, namely the pre-match handshake and exchange of pennants.

articles.title: I was focused on becoming the first Aboriginal tennis champion. Then one remark changed something in me
articles.summary: As a teenager in Sydney, the would-be Wimbledon champion was working towards a singular goal when an act of racism shattered her naivety. It was a regular match. Until it wasn’t. In 1969, I was 17 and had been living in Sydney with my tennis coach, Vic Edwards, and his family for several years.
body: The year before, I had finished high school at Willoughby girls high – where I was the only Aboriginal student – and I was doing my secretarial course in the city. The Metropolitan Business College where I studied was conveniently located near the headquarters of the Foundation for Aboriginal Affairs.

The idea for the foundation was to give city-based Aboriginal people a cultural hub where we could come together and find support. I was spending more and more time there with my friends Isabel and Bob, the latter whom I was casually dating.

Isabel and Bob were young and lots of fun but they were also acutely aware of the politics of being Black. I was naive to the injustices of Australia – and the world – and I learned a lot from Isabel and the guys at the foundation.
At the time, I was focused on a single goal: to become the first Aboriginal tennis champion. To achieve that goal, I had to shut myself off from everything other than tennis. That included politics.

articles.summary: Thomas Tuchel defended England’s record against the world’s leading sides after their 3-2 defeat to Spain, insisting his team have proven they can beat top opposition.
body: The England boss was frustrated by questions over the team’s record against top-ten ranked nations, arguing that similar statistics were not highlighted when his side were winning.
England have now won just six of their past 15 games against top-ten ranked opponents.
“That’s why I was surprised about the World Cup because I think, at the World Cup, we beat three top ten teams,” Tuchel said.
“Interesting that in the moment where we win, nobody brings it up, but when we lose one we come up with statistics.”

articles.title: Spain show their class as errors cost England in Nations League loss
articles.summary: Spain showed why they are the best national team in the world by emerging 3-2 winners from a thrilling, chaotic Nations League clash at Wembley, in which England's flaws undermined their exciting attacking play.
body: It was the World Cup final that might have been had England not squandered their advantage against Argentina this summer - but Spain showed the gap in quality in a result which is a major blow to Thomas Tuchel's stated aim of winning this competition.

Bad errors from Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly helped Lamine Yamal and Alex Baena score Spain's first two and England were cut open through the match, including for Mikel Oyarzabal's winner which came with 16 minutes to play.

Anthony Gordon had urged England to lean into their traditional strengths this week and they did just that with an exceptional counter-attack to make it 1-1, which saw the winger combine with Jude Bellingham before precisely applying the finish. Harry Kane's header from O'Reilly's cross made it 2-1 and capped an incredible transformation in the match.
In four minutes, Spain had conceded more goals than in their eight World Cup games combined.

articles.title: Putellas' first WSL goal helps send London City second with Brighton win
articles.summary: Alexia Putellas scored her first goal in English football, helping London City Lionesses to a 2-0 win against Brighton and sending them second in the WSL table.
body: London City Lionesses vs Brighton and Hove Albion Women. Barclays Women's Super League.

The biggest signing of the summer collected a rebounded save after Chiamaka Nnadozie initially stopped Kadidiatou Diani's strike. She then swerved a half-volley around her defender that beat the still-recovering goalkeeper.

It was the first real chance of a first half that lacked many, although Brighton almost equalised instantly. Emily Murphy's header curled onto the crossbar though and Keiko Seike - who was impressive defensively - could not sort her feet out to slot home the loose ball.

Lucia Corrales rounded off the victory late on, finishing a wonderful team break. Danielle van de Donk stole the ball away from Fran Kirby, releasing Delphine Cascarino, who in turn picked out the incoming run of Corrales on the left, who emphatically finished.

articles.title: Wakefield hailed after stunning Wigan: 'No team would have competed with them!'
articles.summary: Jon Wilkin believes some of the best teams in Super League history would not have beaten Wakefield Trinity on Saturday night, as Daryl Powell's side sealed a huge upset victory against Wigan Warriors to book a spot in the Grand Final.
body: A flurry of second-half tries saw Trinity end Wigan's 16-match winning streak, with the visitors leaving Matt Peet's side stunned by their ferocious pace and power.

Wigan went down to 12 men after 45 minutes, with Adam Keighran being sin-binned for a tip-tackle. Wakefield ruthlessly took advantage, scoring three tries while the Australian five-eighth was off the field.
Wigan did impress in the opening exchanges, matching Wakefield for intensity, with Brad O'Neill breaking the deadlock after a tense first 15 minutes.
But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.
